summary: Allstar One Electric has been folded into Allstar Chargepass (Allstar/Corpay), one card that pays for both fuel and public EV charging. Allstar says it covers more than 100,000 connectors at over 41,000 locations in the UK and Ireland. At most networks drivers tap the card on the charger's RFID reader or start the charge in the Allstar Co-Pilot app, and everything lands on one invoice. Tesla Superchargers are the exception: you add the card as the payment method in the Tesla app, and only Supercharger sites open to other cars can be used by non-Teslas. The network list comes from the operator logos on Allstar's official EV Network Coverage page as of 2026-10-23. A logo does not guarantee that every site of that operator accepts the card, so check single sites with Allstar's Site Locator.

networks.notes: Logo on Allstar coverage page; on-street lamppost chargers (Shell-owned).

networks.name: Tesla Supercharger
networks.notes: Accepted since March 2024, but only by adding the Allstar card in the Tesla app (not by tapping the card). Non-Tesla cars can use only the sites open to other cars.

networks.notes: Logo on Allstar coverage page (motorway services).

networks.name: be.EV
networks.notes: Logo and promotion on Allstar coverage page.

networks.name: Fuuse
networks.notes: Logo on coverage page. Fuuse is a back-office platform used by many small operators, so OSM tags rarely say 'fuuse'.

networks.name: GreenFlux

networks.name: Milence
networks.notes: Logo on coverage page, but under Allstar's separate commercial (HGV/LCV) payment network; some sites are semi-private.

networks.notes: Logo on coverage page; Tap is also a platform/app.

networks.name: Smart Charge
networks.notes: Logo on coverage page (green plug 'Smart Charge' logo, no alt text). Unclear whether this is Sainsbury's Smart Charge or another company with the same name, so the match is low-confidence.

not_listed.notes: Absent from Allstar's coverage page on 2026-10-23, so treat as NOT accepted unless sourced elsewhere: bp pulse (bp chargemaster/polar), Pod Point, char.gy, Sainsbury's Smart Charge (unless it is the 'Smart Charge' logo above). One more logo, a dark 'CHARGE' wordmark with a yellow hexagon icon, could not be identified and is left out.
